questions.q: What does the simple CASE expression compare?
options: Two different tables
One value against a list of exact-match options
Only NULL vs. NOT NULL
Row counts across groups
questions.explain: Simple CASE compares a single expression against a series of WHEN values looking for an exact match.

questions.q: What happens if none of the WHEN values match and there's no ELSE?
options: The result is NULL for that row
SQL Server throws an error
The row is excluded from the results
The first WHEN value is used as a default
questions.explain: ELSE is optional; omitting it means an unmatched row simply gets NULL, which is why this course always includes ELSE.

questions.q: Is CASE a control-flow statement like IF/ELSE?
options: Yes, they work identically
CASE replaces IF/ELSE entirely in T-SQL
CASE can only be used inside stored procedures
No — CASE is an expression that evaluates to one value per row
questions.explain: CASE produces a value and can be used anywhere a value is allowed; IF/ELSE (Chapter 7) controls which block of code runs.

questions.q: Why does a CASE expression typically need an alias?
options: Aliases are required only for the simple form of CASE, not the searched form
Like any calculated expression, it has no natural column name without one
CASE cannot run without an alias
The alias changes which WHEN branch is evaluated
questions.explain: CASE is an expression producing a value per row, just like ListPrice * 0.9 from Lesson 6 — it needs an alias for a readable header.

questions.q: What keyword closes a CASE expression?
options: CLOSE
FINISH
END
STOP
questions.explain: Every CASE expression must be terminated with END.
